text:
maria-wong: Ran the 24h stripe-batching run on the canary cluster. p95 looks fine but p99 for short 128-token requests jumped 2.4x during KV warmups. Notable when requests hit a cold KV shard.
ashok-s: Can you paste the profiler snippet? curious whether it's kernel choice or memcpy/KV plumbing.
maria-wong: Sure — here's the hot path from perf_trace for the 2 p99 samples:
```
# sample 1
call: forward_attn_kernel (float16, fused_qkv=false) -> 1.8ms
kv_fetch: s3-kv-proxy -> 6.4ms
kernel_switch: quantized->fp16 fallback -> +3.2ms
memcpy: device->host (prefetch miss cleanup) -> 2.1ms
# sample 2
call: forward_attn_kernel (int8-quant, fused_qkv=true) -> 1.2ms
kv_fetch: local-ramcache -> 4.9ms
flush-kv-ttl: blocking GC -> 3.6ms
```
lee: That looks like two contributors: external KV latency spike and kernel fallback cost. The quant->fp16 flip costs are worse than I expected for these short sequences (:eyes:).
julia: Any correlation with microbatch size? We previously set microbatch=4 for this run. If KV fetch blocks a single microbatch it holds the whole batch.
maria-wong: microbatch=4, worker threads=8. When a microbatch blocks, avg latency for all requests in that GPU wave shifts. I profiled a subset: when kv_fetch >5ms the scheduler defers new batches but the running microbatch still stalls.
ashok-s: Could we try soft admission: allow in-flight up to N but hold new microbatches until latency budget clears? Example: soft_window=0.8 * target_rps, window_decay on p95 spikes.
julia: I sketched a small algorithm:
```
# pseudo
if observed_p95 > slo_p95: reduce microbatch by 1 (min 1) and set admit_rate *= 0.9
if kv_miss_rate > 0.05: prefetch_topk(prefixes) and mark shard as cold for 30s
if gpu_util > target_high: start shedding low-priority requests at 5% increments
```
lee: Two practical knobs we can tune in the canary: (1) increase microbatch to 6 for throughput baseline, (2) enable soft_admit with headroom target 65% instead of 80%. We should measure cost per token impact.
maria-wong: Perf-bot ran a quick summary on the 24h run: 
```
perf-bot: summary: p50=12ms, p95=42ms, p99=172ms, gpu_util_avg=78%, kv_miss=7.9%, kernel_fallbacks=0.9%
```
ashok-s: If kernel_fallbacks only ~1% they still explain long tails because fallback penalty is multiplicative with kv miss. Two-hit scenario (kv miss + kernel flip) => spike.
julia: Suggest we try two canaries: A) microbatch=6 + headroom=65% + kv-prefetch-on-cold; B) microbatch=3 + soft_admit + conservative kernel-switch threshold. Compare p99, cost.
lee: Also propose adding a short-lived 'warmup' path: when a shard is detected cold, kick async prefetch for first N requests and mark subsequent requests as allowed through soft queue with TTL 15s. That reduces two-hit frequency.
maria-wong: Agree. Action items: 1) I'll spin canary A/B for 6h each. 2) ashok — can you land the soft_admit patch with the window-decay heuristic (small PR, default off)? 3) lee — add KV cold detection metric and prefetch hook. 4) julia — run offline sim for token-cost delta.
julia: I'll also add a micro-sim to model p95->p99 contribution of the fallback cost; should be quick.
perf-bot: note: scheduled canary runs at 1977655400 and 1977659000. Results will be auto-posted to this thread. :rocket:
maria-wong: thanks all — let's minimize the two-hit scenario and aim for stable p99 <= 1.6x p95.
lee: SGTM. If canaries look good we roll to staging with 1% traffic for 24h. :+1:
